assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin-based therapy is a rare combination of mechanistic discovery (incretin effect, proglucagon processing, GLP-1 actions on islets, gut and brain) and transformative clinical impact in type 2 diabetes and obesity, with effects now reaching cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Originality and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed across physiology (Holst, Drucker), peptide identification and chemistry (Mojsov) and drug development (Knudsen). A prize for the discovery of GLP-1 biology fits three laureates, but the exact allocation, including the relative role of Mojsov and of other early investigators not on the list, is unresolved. The choice of Mojsov over Knudsen is a judgment on discovery versus engineering.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and large randomized outcome trials; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue given the public health impact.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among discoverers of the active peptide is disputed and the list may omit relevant contributors.
Whether the committee prefers recognising drug development (Knudsen) alongside physiology is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The concept is original, clinically validated and widely extended, including to autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June contributed key CAR design (costimulation) and first clinical translation; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early clinical CAR trials. Other foundational contributors (e.g. Eshhar, Kuwana) are not in the supplied credit, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade-plus of follow-up; limitations in solid tumours and toxicity remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept lies partly outside the supplied names.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, a signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing), defined a fundamental principle of proteostasis with relevance for diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and aging. Originality and clarity are excellent.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and decisively elucidated the pathway; two laureates is a clean configuration. Other contributors to early ER stress signalling (e.g. Kaufman, Ron) are not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and well confirmed across species; direct therapeutic translation is still emerging, but the basic discovery stands firmly.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation (e.g. ISR modulators) is not yet established.
Treatment of the PERK/ATF6 arms and related investigators is not covered by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR/mTOR as a central regulator of growth and nutrient response links basic cell biology to cancer, metabolism, immunology and aging, and underpins rapalog therapies. The conceptual impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and defined it as a growth regulator; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and key pathway components; Schreiber contributed to the rapamycin target chemistry. Hall plus Sabatini is a defensible pair, but Schreiber's and others' (e.g. Brown, Sabers) roles complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and clinical use of mTOR inhibitors; the field is mature, though some clinical expectations (anti-aging, oncology) remain partial.
uncertainties: Competing claims on identification of the mammalian target.
Clinical impact is narrower than the mechanistic impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level data showing large reductions in precancer and invasive cervical cancer. The cause-to-prevention chain is compelling and has major global health value.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs; Frazer contributed to VLP vaccine development in parallel with Zhou; the zur Hausen Nobel recognised the HPV-cancer link. Credit may also involve Jian Zhou (deceased), not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Now supported by registry-level cancer incidence data; recognition is timely as long-term effects on cervical cancer emerge.
uncertainties: Priority among parallel VLP developers is partly contested.
Interaction with the earlier prize for HPV-cancer causation could be seen as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with impact on antiviral defence, autoinflammatory disease, autoimmunity and cancer immunotherapy. Original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber identified STING. This forms a natural two-person prize, though other contributors (Vance, Ishikawa, Sun, Wu in the supplied credits) complicate the picture.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed; therapeutic application remains largely preclinical or early clinical, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not yet proven.
Allocation among several groups that contributed to STING discovery is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics transformed experimental neuroscience and physiology by enabling causal control of defined cell populations; channelrhodopsin discovery and its neuronal application are original and enormously influential.
assessment.attribution: Six credited names. Nagel and Hegemann characterised channelrhodopsin function; Deisseroth, Boyden and others adapted it to neurons; Miesenböck and Bamberg have distinct claims. Any trio leaves out credible contributors, so allocation is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and ubiquitous in research; clinical translation is just beginning (e.g. vision restoration), so the medical dimension is more limited.
uncertainties: Contested priority between channelrhodopsin discovery and its neuronal deployment.
Limited direct medical impact so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Positional cloning of leptin revealed an adipocyte-derived hormone controlling appetite and body weight, founding modern molecular understanding of energy homeostasis and explaining monogenic obesity. Foundational and clear.
assessment.attribution: Only Friedman is supplied; the work built on Coleman's parabiosis studies and collaborations with Leibel, and the leptin receptor work involved others, so a sole award would omit relevant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature; clinical utility is mostly confined to lipodystrophy and leptin deficiency, but the conceptual impact is lasting.
uncertainties: Sole credit may be unfair to collaborators and to earlier parabiosis work.
Limited broad therapeutic payoff for common obesity.
